title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan Sign a 'Shield of Peace' Defense Pact
summary: What if three countries promised to treat an attack on one as an attack on all? That's exactly what happened on Friday in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. The leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the "Makkah Joint Defence Agreement." They held up green and red folders with fresh signatures for the cameras. The pact says if any of the three nations is attacked, the other two will come to its defense. The leaders called it a "shield of peace" and said it's not aimed at any specific country. But many experts believe it's really about Iran. Right now, the U.S. and Israel are at war with Iran, and missiles and drones have already hit nearby countries, including Saudi Arabia. This new deal builds on an older one between just Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, signed last year. Adding Turkey brings in a strong military that uses NATO-standard equipment. Analysts say the pact is more of a warning signal than a ready-to-fight alliance. It could take years to build a combined military force. The agreement doesn't name an enemy, which one expert said was done on purpose — it creates uncertainty for anyone thinking of attacking. The three countries have been working together on defense since at least 2022. Pakistan's former ambassador said other nations like Egypt, Qatar, and Kuwait have shown interest in joining. For now, the pact is a big statement: these three Muslim-majority nations are standing together in a dangerous neighborhood.
why_it_matters: If these three countries became involved in a bigger war, it could change fuel prices around the world and affect the safety of millions of kids and families in the Middle East.

keywords.explanation: A promise between countries to help each other if one of them is attacked.
The holiest city in the religion of Islam, located in Saudi Arabia.
A phrase used by the leaders to describe their new agreement, meaning they hope it will protect them and prevent war.
Military tools and weapons made to match the high-quality rules used by NATO, a big group of countries that defend each other.
A feeling of not knowing what will happen, which can make an enemy think twice before starting a fight.
When most of the people living in a country follow the religion of Islam.

background_read: Saudi Arabia and Iran have been rivals in the Middle East for many years, backing different sides in wars in Yemen, Syria, and other places. Saudi Arabia sees Iran's growing military power as a big threat.

Turkey is a member of NATO (a group of 32 countries that promise to defend each other), so its army uses advanced Western equipment. Pakistan has nuclear weapons and a large army that has helped Saudi Arabia train its forces for decades.

The pact is called the "Makkah Joint Defence Agreement" because it was signed in Mecca (also spelled Makkah), Islam's most sacred city, which gives it special symbolic meaning for the three Muslim-majority nations involved.
Article_Structure: WHO: The leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan.
WHAT: They signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, which says an attack on one will be treated as an attack on all three.
WHERE: In the holy city of Mecca, Saudi Arabia.
WHY: Officially as a "shield of peace," but most experts see it as a message to Iran during a time of war and drone attacks in the region.

perspectives.description: Say the deal is purely for peace and protection, not aimed at any particular country, and will help bring stability to the Muslim world.
Point out that without a combined military force ready right away, the pact is more of a warning than a real defense, but it could grow stronger over time.
Likely see this as an unfriendly move that could make the region even more divided, but the pact's vagueness might also make them more cautious about attacking.
